findings.reportedText: F01 · High · Currency-pair quote units are misleading B / C USD/JPY displays a dollar-prefixed exchange-rate number, including “$148.5200” in the order panel. The Markets forex table applies the same dollar formatting to non-USD quote currencies. USD/JPY is yen per US dollar; EUR/GBP is pounds per euro. A dollar sign on these rates confuses the currency being measured. The simulator may intentionally use simplified instrument accounting, but that does not teach actual spot-FX units. No submitted order was used to test conversion or P&L. Recommended: Display the actual quote currency beside the rate, define the base-unit quantity, and explain separately how any simplified virtual instrument maps into the USD account. Verify its accounting in an authorized test environment. Financial clarity issue, not an established deceptive-practices violation. F1 supplies the counterevidence for the unit convention. findings.reportedText: F03 · Medium · Chart, order quote and market-directory values can disagree B / C In the USD/JPY observation, the chart showed $155.0501 while the order panel showed $148.5200. In a later screenshot the headline and order value matched, while generated chart history still followed a different path. BTC also showed distinct chart and order values in an early capture. The pages disclose separate provenance, simulated candles and different intervals. This is not evidence of a wrong fill. Nevertheless, a beginner can read the chart as the price available to the order panel. The listed URLs are the shared component scope; a price mismatch was directly documented only in the named examples. Recommended: Put separate Chart input and Virtual execution input labels immediately beside both values, with observation times. Explain fixed versus generated values before a first order. Avoid presenting synthetic history as a tradeable historical series. B/C usability and trust issue. No intentional deception or inaccurate execution is established. findings.reportedText: F04 · Medium · Several learning tasks require capabilities or external datasets absent from the terminal B / C These explanations disclose that standard historical RSI, MACD, VWAP, volume profiles or derivatives execution are not implemented. Yet repeated Apply This in the Simulator or Practise this strategy calls lead to the generic terminal. The disclosures prevent a straightforward false-feature finding. The remaining gap is pedagogical: a learner is directed to a tool that cannot perform the described comparison without additional data or a worksheet. Recommended: Offer a small, complete downloadable or on-page worked dataset and direct the CTA to the supported arithmetic exercise. Distinguish conceptual lesson from terminal practice at the CTA itself. B/C expectation and beginner-experience concern; unsupported features are explicitly disclosed.
